newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador court asks U.S. envoy to explain charges.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador court asks U.S. envoy to explain charges.

text.p: The President of Ecuador's Supreme Court said on Monday he had asked the United States ambassador to explain to the court allegations he made about drug trafficking and corruption by some judges.
"I am going to summon the whole Supreme Court to hear the ambassador's declarations Wednesday," Carlos Solorzano told reporters.

It was not immediately clear whether the ambassador, Leslie Alexander, would take up Solorzano's invitation. He recently accused "some judges" in the country's legal system of being involved in drug trafficking.
The allegations led to a wave of protests, including criticism from President Fabian Alarcon who asked Alexander not to meddle in Ecuador's internal affairs.
Ecuador's legislators, who designate the country's judges, asked Alexander to explain his declarations.
"One cannot say that the legal system has these problems. If one makes these affirmations one has to come with proof," Mauro Landazuri, a member of congress from the Democratic Left Party, said.
Alexander has become outspoken about internal matters in Ecuador. In February he made accusations of irregularities in the customs services and described Ecuador as a country riddled with corruption.
He made the statements a few days before Congress ousted former President Abdala Bucaram. Bucaram's six months in power brought with it a large amount of criticism of corruption.
